M1.reason: Outline is a flat rectangular case, low and wide, matching the brief's lying-flat case. The front, back, left and right views all show the same slab profile, and the carry handle is the only thing standing proud of it, as the brief asks.

M2.reason: Measured 35 x 26 x 7 units against the brief's 35 long, 26 wide and 7 high, with zero error.

M3.reason: Parts the brief names: the case, the red cross on the top (centred, upright in the top view) and one carry handle (a black bar with rounded ends, on the top, reading in the left and right views). No small part is missing. The brief names no claws, teeth, rivets or round parts.

M4.reason: Case is a light grey-white painted surface, close enough to the brief's white. Cross is red and the handle is black, as the brief asks. Materials read as painted metal throughout, with no region in a wrong colour.

M5.reason: The brief's 'a little scuffed' is there: pale chipped highlights along the top and bottom edges of the case, and a fine worn grain over the top. The cross and handle are crisp. Nothing is smeared.

M6.reason: In lineup.png (D) it reads as a plausible first-aid pickup at a glance: a red cross, a handle, a flat case. Up close it is cleaner and more uniform than Half-Life's own grimy props (the crowbar, the shotgun), and its grey is cooler and flatter. A player might take it for a game model, but not for certain.

M7.reason: It lies flat on its base, with the cross upright and the handle on the far side in the top view. The brief gives no front, so the facing is a sensible reading of a flat pickup, and it is set on its origin.

M8.reason: The check passes with no errors. It has 72 triangles, against a median of 62 for Half-Life props of this kind and size, well under twice that. The handle sits on the top surface in the front-left and back-left views, and nothing is open or floating.
